lesson_title: Springs, Spray Paint and a Delivery Truck: Physics Exam Essentials
hook_text: The apple pulls the Earth EXACTLY as hard as the Earth pulls the apple. Same force. So why does only the apple fall?
clip_script: Newton's third law stops being spooky the moment you see forces as two-ended springs. A spring never pushes at one end only — compress it and BOTH ends push outward, stretch it and both ends pull inward. Every force in nature is such a spring between two objects: the Earth pulls the falling apple and the apple pulls the Earth, with exactly equal force. The apple moves more because it is lighter, not because it is pulled harder — same spring, different masses on the ends.
visual_style: A glowing spring stretched between a tiny apple and the whole Earth; force arrows of identical length on both ends; the apple streaking downward while the Earth shifts by a hair, with a zoom-in proving it moved.
mood: Mind-flip wonder — the law everyone recites and almost nobody believes, made obvious.
pacing: Slow reveal of the spring, the equal-arrows beat held for effect, then the punchline of the Earth's imperceptible budge.
